text:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding sample app is still causing duplicate side-effects when a client hits a 429 and then immediately refreshes the token + retries. Seen in two customer trials. stack: node-sdk + hosted API. anyone seen similar?

kevin: yep saw one yesterday in the sandbox. pattern looks like: client gets 429, refresh rotates token, client retried the original request without an idempotency key -> downstream created duplicate resource.

sam: oof. is the SDK setting any default idempotency header? iirc node SDK left that opt-in last time.

maria: not by default for the sample app. we intentionally kept it minimal for onboarding. but maybe that's a bad tradeoff for production-like behavior.

tay: quick question: are these immediate retries using aggressive retry windows (no jitter)? if so adding jitter + backoff might reduce the double-send frequency.

kevin: confirmed — sample app uses linear retry 200ms, 500ms, 1000ms, no jitter. also token refresh flow does an early retry on 401 that races with the queued retry for 429.

sam: proposal: three changes: 1) add default idempotency-key header in sample app (+ docs), 2) switch to exponential backoff with full jitter, 3) emit telemetry event when we detect a duplicate side-effect so we can quantify.

maria: sounds reasonable. for (1) should sample app use a simple UUID per user action? we don't want to push a dev to manage dedupe serverside but show best practices.

tay: yes — generate a v4 uuid per logical operation and show server-side dedupe example in the sample server code. also show the header name we recommend: `Idempotency-Key`.

kevin: for (2) let's use the AWS-style full jitter: sleep = random_between(0, base * 2^attempt). base=150ms (?) to avoid huge initial delay. snippet for node: 
```
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))
const backoff = (attempt) => Math.floor(Math.random() * (150 * Math.pow(2, attempt)))
await sleep(backoff(attempt))
```

sam: +1. also handle the token-rotation race: when we see 401 followed by a successful refresh, SDK should avoid immediately replaying queued 429 retries until refresh completes and the retry uses the fresh token. basically enqueue and rehydrate retries with latest auth token.

maria: that will require parity across SDKs — node, python, go. we should document the handshake: refresh -> broadcast token event -> retry queue drains with new token. otherwise clients do: refresh -> new token but parallel previous retry used old token or old idempotency keys.

kevin: telemetry: add two events: `retry.attempt` (with attempt_count, error_code, route, sampled=true/false) and `retry.duplicate_detected` (triggered when server signals dedupe or when we observe downstream idempotency conflict). sample app should surface counts at /metrics.

tay: suggestion: sample 1% of requests for full payload in telemetry to keep costs down, but always increment counters for retry types. also add a debug flag in sample app to enable verbose logs for onboarding sessions.

sam: devex-bot: I can wire a quick checklist into the sample app PR template. Checklist items: default Idempotency-Key, exponential+full-jitter backoff, queued-retries-wait-for-refresh, telemetry counters, docs snippet for server dedupe.

devex-bot: noted. assigned to @maria for patching sample app and @kevin for SDK retry logic update. Please link PRs here when ready. :white_check_mark:

maria: i'll open a draft PR today for the sample app changes and a follow-up issue that lists SDK parity tasks. will include a small test that reproduces the race (script that forces 429 then rotates token).

kevin: i'll prototype the queued-retry token handshake in node and python SDKs. will ping infra for a short canary on staging.

tay: can we add a tiny e2e script in the onboarding flow? something like `scripts/fuzz-retry.sh` that simulates 429+token-rotation race so new hires can reproduce.

maria: yes — good training tool. thanks all.

sam: one last minor UX ask: update the onboarding README to call out "This sample app enables idempotency by default to demonstrate safe retries" so fewer people copy the minimal insecure pattern.

maria: agreed. i'll include that. closing the thread once PRs link here. :sparkles:
